exercises.name: Agility Ladder Icky Shuffle
instructions: Stand to the left of the first square in an athletic stance with hips and knees slightly bent.
Step the right foot into the square, then the left foot in beside it.
Step the right foot out to the right of the ladder, then bring the left foot forward into the next square.
Follow with the right foot in, step the left foot out to the left, and keep the in-in-out rhythm zig-zagging up the ladder.
exercises.formCue: In, in, out. Stay on the balls of your feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Staring at the feet and standing tall, or rushing the pattern before the rhythm is clean.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk the pattern slowly and say the steps out loud until it is automatic, then add speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains fast, coordinated weight shifts from side to side while still moving forward.

exercises.name: Agility Ladder Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Stand side-on at one end of the ladder with both feet in the first square, knees soft and chest over toes.
Shift your weight to the trailing leg and step the lead foot into the next square.
Bring the trailing foot in to join it without crossing your feet.
Travel the full ladder, then return leading with the other foot.
exercises.formCue: Hips low, feet quick, never cross.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bobbing up and down with each step, or letting the feet click together and cross.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow to a walk and use one foot contact per square before adding the second.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Quick lateral steps from a low stance are the base of defending and changing direction.

exercises.name: L-Drill
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hamstrings, calves, hip stabilisers
instructions: Set three cones in an L shape with about 5 yards between each cone.
Sprint from the first cone to the second, touch the line, and sprint back to the first.
Sprint back to the second cone, round it tightly, and weave around the inside of the third cone.
Round the third cone, come back around the second, and finish through the first cone.
exercises.formCue: Short choppy steps into the cone, lean, then go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up tall at the cones and taking wide looping turns.
exercises.beginnerModification: Jog the route at half speed until the path is memorised, then build pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses braking, tight turning and re-accelerating in one short effort.

source.name: NSCA, Developing Agility and Quickness (Human Kinetics excerpt)

exercises.name: Falling Start
instructions: Stand tall with feet under your hips and eyes straight ahead.
Keep your body in one straight line and let yourself tip forward from the ankles.
At the point where you must step, drive one knee forward hard and punch the opposite arm.
Push the ground back behind you and accelerate for 10 to 20 metres, rising gradually.
exercises.formCue: Fall as a plank, then drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist instead of leaning as one line, or stepping out too early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from a staggered stance with a smaller lean and run at three-quarter speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the forward body lean and first-step drive that acceleration depends on.

source.name: Human Kinetics, Three Drills for Developing Starts and Initial Acceleration

exercises.name: Resisted Sled Sprint
instructions: Attach the harness to a lightly loaded sled and walk forward until the strap is tight.
Set a staggered stance with a forward lean from the ankles.
Drive out and sprint 10 to 20 metres, pushing the ground back with each step.
Keep the same lean and arm action you would use in an unloaded start, then walk back and rest fully.
exercises.formCue: Lean and push. Same shape as a free sprint.
exercises.commonMistakes: Loading the sled so heavy that the stride turns into a grind and posture breaks.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light sled or sprint up a gentle slope instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A light towing load builds the horizontal push used in the first steps of a sprint.

source.name: NSCA Coach, Sled Resisted Sprint Training

exercises.name: Sprint and Stop
instructions: Place two cones 10 to 15 metres apart.
Accelerate from the first cone at a controlled, fast pace.
As you near the second cone, lower your hips and shorten your steps, bending at the ankles, knees and hips on each contact.
Come to a balanced stop at the cone in an athletic stance and hold for two seconds.
exercises.formCue: Sink the hips, chop the steps, own the stop.
exercises.commonMistakes: Braking with stiff, upright legs or leaning back on the heels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Run at half speed and allow more steps to slow down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Being able to brake under control comes before every cut and change of direction.

source.name: NSCA, Effective Deceleration Technique for Court and Field Sports

exercises.name: Snap-Down
instructions: Stand tall on your toes with both arms reaching overhead.
Pull your arms down fast and let your feet leave the floor slightly.
Land on both feet at once with hips back, knees bent and chest over your knees.
Hold the landing position for two seconds, then stand and reset.
exercises.formCue: Snap down and freeze.
exercises.commonMistakes: Knees caving inward or landing stiff and loud.
exercises.beginnerModification: Skip the hop and simply drop quickly from tall into the landing position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the landing position at low impact before any real jumping.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Drop Landing
instructions: Stand on a low box, about 15 to 30 cm high.
Step off the edge without jumping up.
Land on both feet together, hips back, knees bent and in line with your toes.
Hold the landing for two seconds before stepping back up.
exercises.formCue: Step off, land quiet, stick it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping up off the box, or letting the knees collapse inward on contact.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower step, or go back to the snap-down.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the ability to absorb force from a height before rebound jumps are added.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop and Stick
instructions: Balance on one leg with a soft knee.
Hop forward a short distance and land on the same leg.
Absorb the landing with hip and knee bent, knee over the middle of the foot.
Hold still for two seconds, then reset and repeat before switching legs.
exercises.formCue: Small hop, quiet landing, hold.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hopping too far, wobbling at the knee, or letting the hip drop on landing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hop from two feet and land on one, or shorten the hop to a few centimetres.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Most sport landings and cuts happen on one leg, so control has to be trained on one leg.

source.name: NSCA, Plyometric Implementation: Jump Landing Positions

exercises.name: Hurdle Hop
instructions: Line up low hurdles about a metre apart and stand facing the first one.
Jump off both feet over the first hurdle, pulling the toes up in the air.
Land on both feet at the same time and rebound straight into the next jump.
Keep ground contacts short and the torso tall through the full row, then walk back.
exercises.formCue: Both feet together. Bounce, do not sink.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sinking deep into each landing, or landing one foot after the other.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use mini hurdles or lines on the floor and pause to reset between jumps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeated rebounds train the quick, springy ground contact used in sprinting and jumping.

source.name: ISBS Conference Proceedings, Kinetic Analysis of Horizontal Plyometric Exercise Intensity

exercises.name: Alternate Leg Push-Off
instructions: Place one foot flat on a low box with the other foot on the floor.
Drive through the box foot and swing your arms to jump straight up.
Switch legs in the air so the other foot lands on the box.
Land softly with hips back and knees bent, then go again.
exercises.formCue: Drive up through the box foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing mostly off the floor foot, or landing heavily with a locked knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pause and reset between jumps, or use a lower step.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It develops single-leg drive in the same alternating rhythm as running.

exercises.name: Forward Hurdle Run
instructions: Line up mini hurdles roughly a stride apart and start in a staggered stance.
Run through with one foot landing between each pair of hurdles.
Lift each knee to about hip height and swing the opposite arm from the shoulder.
Stay tall with your trunk braced until you are past the last hurdle.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, toe up, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back or looking down, which shortens the knee lift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk or march over the hurdles first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It grooves knee lift, rhythm and upright posture for faster running.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound to Shot-Put Throw
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall, a few metres away, holding a light medicine ball at your chest.
Bound sideways away from the wall and land on the outside leg, loading the hip.
Push back off that leg, rotate your hips and trunk toward the wall.
Finish by punching the ball from the back shoulder into the wall, then collect it and reset.
exercises.formCue: Load the hip, turn, then throw.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing with the arm only, or losing balance on the landing before the throw.
exercises.beginnerModification: Remove the bound and throw from a split stance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links a sideways push off the ground to a rotational throw, as in striking and throwing sports.

source.name: NSCA, Strength Training for Lacrosse (Human Kinetics excerpt)

exercises.name: Plant and Cut
instructions: Jog four or five steps in a straight line.
Plant on the outside foot with the knee bent and in line with the toes.
Push off that foot to change direction diagonally.
Accelerate for five to seven quick steps, slow down, and repeat off the other foot.
exercises.formCue: Plant under the hip, knee over toes, go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the planted knee buckle inward, or cutting with an upright trunk.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk into the plant and make the angle of the cut shallow.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It rehearses the cutting step with good knee position at a controlled speed.

exercises.name: Quick Forward-Backward Run
instructions: Set a line of cones about 5 metres apart.
Run forward quickly two cones.
Run backward one cone with hips and knees slightly bent and small quick steps.
Keep repeating two forward, one back until the end of the line, then jog back.
exercises.formCue: Small fast steps, hips low going back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing upright and leaning back while backpedalling.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at a jog and shorten the cone spacing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains quick transitions between forward running and backpedalling.

exercises.name: Squat with Toe Raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Sit back slowly until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees, keeping them in line with your toes.
Stand up a little faster than you went down.
Once your legs are straight, rise onto your toes, then lower the heels and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Slow down, knees out, finish tall on the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Knees drifting inward on the way down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a shallower depth and hold a support for the toe raise.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It pairs knee-control practice with calf strength in one simple warm-up move.

exercises.name: Running Hip Out
instructions: Jog easily in a straight line.
Every few steps, pause and lift one knee forward to hip height.
Rotate that knee out to the side, then put the foot down.
Jog on and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Knee up, open the gate.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the trunk instead of moving at the hip.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it walking with a hand on a wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the hips and wakes up single-leg balance before faster running.

exercises.name: Running Hip In
instructions: Jog easily in a straight line.
Every few steps, pause and lift one knee out to the side at hip height.
Rotate that knee inward to the front, then put the foot down.
Jog on and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.formCue: Knee out, close the gate.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning the body away from the lifted leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it walking with a hand on a wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It prepares the inner hip and groin for cutting and kicking.

exercises.name: Partner Mirror Drill
instructions: Set two cones about 5 metres apart and face your partner between them.
One athlete leads, shuffling left and right between the cones and changing direction at random.
The other athlete mirrors every move, staying square and directly opposite.
Work for about 10 seconds, rest, then swap roles.
exercises.formCue: Watch the hips, stay low, stay square.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet or guessing instead of reacting.
exercises.beginnerModification: Have the leader move at half speed with clearer changes of direction.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Reacting to another person is closer to real sport than any pre-planned cone pattern.

source.name: National Association of Speed and Explosion

exercises.name: Ball Drop Reaction
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance a few metres from a partner who holds a tennis ball at shoulder height.
The partner drops the ball without warning.
Sprint and catch the ball before it bounces a second time.
Walk back and reset, and increase the distance as you get faster.
exercises.formCue: Eyes on the ball, first step low.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall while waiting, or reaching with the hands instead of moving the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start closer to the partner.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a fast first step in response to something you see, not a planned start.

source.name: NSCA, 5 Reaction Drills to Build Quickness

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat Touchdown
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip stabilisers, ankle stabilisers
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot hovering just in front or to the side.
Brace your trunk and sit back into a single-leg squat.
Lower until the toes of the free leg lightly touch the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to return to the top, and finish all reps before switching.
exercises.formCue: Touch like the floor is hot. Weight stays on the standing leg.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing knee collapsing inward, or putting real weight through the touching foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a support with one hand and squat to a shallower depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds single-leg strength and knee control without needing any load.

exercises.name: Kneeling Wood Chop
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band with high anchor
instructions: Set a cable at its highest position and kneel side-on to it with the inside leg forward and the outside knee down.
Grip the rope with both hands, reaching up toward the anchor.
Pull the rope diagonally across your body down to the outside hip.
Keep the torso tall and hips still, pause, and return under control.
exercises.formCue: Tall spine, hips quiet, arms draw the line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending or twisting from the lower back, or letting the hips swing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light band and shorten the range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The kneeling stance takes the legs out so the trunk has to control the diagonal pull.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hay Baler
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band with low anchor
instructions: Set a cable at its lowest position and kneel side-on to it with the outside leg forward and the inside knee down.
Grip the rope with both hands beside the inside hip.
Pull the rope up to your chest, then press it up and across in front of the far shoulder.
Pause for a second at the top with your torso still, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Pull to the chest, press across, body stays still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning away from the machine or shrugging the load up with the arms only.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load, or the medicine-ball version.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A low-to-high diagonal pull trains the trunk to pass force upward, as in throwing and swinging.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Medicine Ball Hay Baler
instructions: Kneel with one foot forward and the other knee on the floor.
Hold a medicine ball in both hands beside the hip of the back leg.
Turn your trunk and shoulders to sweep the ball across your body and over the opposite shoulder.
Lower it back along the same path, and finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.formCue: Eyes follow the ball. Hips face forward.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the arms without turning the trunk, or wobbling at the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter ball or no ball at all.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a simple entry to diagonal trunk rotation with a stable base.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge Wood Chop
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band at shoulder height
instructions: Set a cable at shoulder height and stand side-on to it holding the handle in both hands near the inside shoulder.
Step sideways away from the machine into a lateral lunge.
As the foot lands, keep your arms long and rotate to bring the handle down toward the lunging leg.
Push off that foot and rotate back to the start.
exercises.formCue: Step, sit, chop. One smooth move.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to reach down, or letting the lunging knee cave in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the lateral lunge and the standing chop separately first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It ties a sideways step to trunk rotation, the way cutting and reaching happen in sport.

exercises.name: Anti-Rotation Reverse Lunge
exercises.equipment: Cable machine or band at chest height
instructions: Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to it with feet hip-width apart.
Hold the handle in both hands and press your arms straight out in front of your chest.
Step the leg nearest the machine back into a lunge, lowering the knee toward the floor.
Keep the hands in front of your breastbone the whole time, then push through the front foot to stand.
exercises.formCue: Hands stay on the centre line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the cable turn the shoulders, or leaning toward the machine.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold the press-out standing still first, then add a shallow lunge.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the trunk to resist twisting while the legs move, which is how the core works in running and cutting.
